source_references.readback:
For $\Re s>1$, absolute convergence and unique factorization give
$$
-\zeta'(s)/\zeta(s)=s/(s-1)+s\int_1^\infty(\psi(t)-t)t^{-s-1}\,dt.
$$
The compact part before $e^{200}$ is harmless; the rest is normally
convergent on every compact subset of $\Re s>b$ by A. Thus the
right side continues holomorphically there except at 1. The identity
theorem and the nonzero residue of the logarithmic derivative at a zero
give $\beta \le b$ for each nontrivial zero. This is a **closed upper
cap**, not a proof of exclusion at $b$. The zeta continuation and
symmetries are the standard ones used in the allowed FKS §2 and CH2
Appendices A/B. No real zero in $0<s<1$ occurs: the alternating
Dirichlet series for $(1-2^{1-s})\zeta(s)$ is positive by pairing.
Count multiplicities throughout. This is why several improvements
start before $e^{200}$: the hypothesis controls an analytic
continuation globally; it is not directly evaluated below its threshold.

source_references.readback:
Let $H=3000175332800, h=\log H$. By Platt–Trudgian FiniteRH
Theorem 1 (original PDF p.2; announcement p.1), off-line zeros
of positive ordinate have ordinate at least $H$. Below we use
$H$ as a lower integration limit, so also allowing equality causes
no issue. Put $s_* =.72$. For $s\ge s_*$ in our screens let
$p=8(1-s)/3, q=5-2s$. Use the **first** FKS Table 8 panel
(PDF p.26, Cor. 2.9 and (2.17), pp.7–8) on its own interval, or
Dusart Theorem 2.3 (PDF p.5), to write a density bound
$$
N(s,t)\le c t^p(\log t)^q+d(\log t)^2\quad(t\ge H).
$$
FKS Remark 1.5(2), PDF p.3, explicitly distinguishes the
adopted .77 input from the announced .618 value (“if and when
… confirmed”). The latter is not imported or established from A here.
Use the stated interval corollary at original-paper trust, not a
new invocation of Thm. 2.7 with the separately displayed delta
parameter. For Dusart use $c=4.9\cdot3^p,d=51.5$ by $\log(1+v)\le v$.
Table constants are rounded **up** in `d02screen.py`; bounds are
minimized as whole bounds, not mixing coefficients. Changing the
integration limit does not change the $H_0=3\cdot10^{12}$ of the
FKS Table 8 parameters. The density results need not be reoptimized
at unmatched parameters. Whether an original includes $\beta=s$
does not matter; the cumulative mass below uses $\beta>s$.

For $m=1,2$ bound the two-sided mass
$2\sum_{\gamma>0, \beta>s}\gamma^{-m}$ by
$2m\int_H^\infty N(s,t)t^{-m-1}dt$. Put $\lambda=m-p>0,z=\lambda h$,
$$
A_z=\sum_{j=0}^3{3\choose j}j!/z^j,\qquad
B_z=\sum_{j=0}^3{3\choose j}(j+1)!/z^{j+1}.
$$
The bound per source is
$$
W_m(s;c,d)=
\frac{2mc e^{-z}h^q}{\lambda} A_z(1+B_z/A_z)^{q-3}
+2d e^{-mh}(h^2+2h/m+2/m^2).
$$
Indeed $t=H e^v$; with weight $e^{-\lambda v}(1+v/h)^3\,dv$,
the mean of $v/h$ is $B_z/A_z$. Concavity of
$(1+v/h)^{q-3}$ (here $3<q<4$) gives the displayed Jensen
upper bound. This also applies to the $m=2$ integral, instead of
merely dividing the $m=1$ bound by $H$.

source_references.readback:
Take nodes from $s_*$ to $b$ of step .00025. At each node below the
last one take the upward rounding of the min of the source values,
then the running minimum $w_j$ to preserve monotonicity. A preceding
upper bound for the tail is still valid later. For all but the last bin
use the left cumulative bound $w_j$; equivalently assign mass
$w_j-w_{j+1}$ at the right endpoint for estimating increasing
weights. For the last bin, from $s_{J-1}$ to $b$, use the
**linear chord** of the Dusart integral between its two upper endpoint
values $w_{J-1}$ and $w_b$. The checker verifies that at the left
it is indeed the selected upper value, and that it decreases. This
chord bounds the true Dusart majorant: each integrand in its first
term is a positive constant times an exponential of an affine
function of $s$ $because (p,q) are affine$; the second term is
constant. Hence the actual integrated majorant is convex. Avoid
an artificial atom of size $w_{J-1}-w_b$ at $b$: spread it
uniformly over this last bin, retaining $w_b$ at $b$.
Define $B_m(L)$ as the sum of the masses just specified times
$e^{-(b-s)L}$, with the uniform mass term integrated:
$$
 B_m(L)=\sum_{j<J-1}(w_j-w_{j+1})e^{-(b-s_{j+1})L}
 +w_b+(w_{J-1}-w_b)\frac{1-e^{-(b-s_{J-1})L}}{(b-s_{J-1})L}.
$$
This dominates the exponentially weighted actual mass by layer-cake
integration in $s$. At nodes any jump conventions in the auxiliary
majorant can be taken right-continuous; the true **strict** tail and
the value at $s_*$ are bounded. The $w_b$ term is an upper
allowance for a possible boundary atom, not an assertion it exists.
All terms are nonnegative and nonincreasing in $L$.
The chord is materially relevant to the limiting coefficient.
The limiting allowances satisfy $w_b<.116297$ for $m=1$ and
$w_b<2.506\cdot10^{-14}$ for $m=2$ (both strict). The same
routine with cap $7/8$ is an optional within-method B0 comparison,
not a replacement of any stronger inherited B0 branch.

**New multiple-chord majorant for $m=1$.**
At each regular bin $[s_j,s_{j+1})$, denote its two rounded
running-minimum endpoints by $w_j,w_{j+1}$. Whenever they
equal the upward-rounded Jensen estimates of the **same**
source with the same table block (for Dusart, same formula),
replace the constant tail majorant in the bin by the straight
line through these values. Convexity of the *exact moment
integral* of the chosen density bound proves this line is an
upper bound, whether or not the Jensen formula itself is
convex. Otherwise keep the old constant envelope with the
right-edge step. Equality of the rounded endpoints with a
particular source is checked by integer comparisons in
`chords()`; if any running min came from a previous node,
this rule is equally safe. At the cap keep the same last
Dusart chord and atom. The resulting decreasing tail gives
a positive measure supported in $[s_*,b]$, with weights
$w_j-w_{j+1}$ spread uniformly in selected bins and at the
right endpoints otherwise. Each of the selected uniform
contributions replaces $e^{-(b-r)L}$ at the right node $r$
by $e^{-(b-r)L}(1-e^{-(r-l)L})/[(r-l)L]$. The new
coefficient $B_1^\sharp$ is nonincreasing and no larger than
the old licensed $B_1$; they have the same terminal allowance.
The code uses a grouped Horner evaluation. The method bounds
the weighted **strict** zero tail on the entire strip by layer
integration; it neither assumes zero-free table joins nor removes
possible zeros at the cap. We continue to use the original
licensed $B_2$ for smoothing.

source_references.readback:
Let $T=e^{c_*L}$ with $c_*=7/20$, $y=c_*L+1$. From $L=155$
use FKS Thm. 3.2 (PDF p.8) with the row
$(\log x_M,\alpha,\omega,M)=(40,1/2,0,2.091)$.
The two admissibility inequalities $T>\max(51,L)$ and
$5T+2<e^{L/2}$ hold at 155 and persist (the ratios of
the exponential to each competing term increase).
The formula gives a possibly different $T^*$ at every
argument; $T\le T^*\le2.45T<e^y$. No prime-power midpoint
convention is substituted for this original signed formula
on its real domain. See FKS Remark 3.3 for the stated provenance;
we do not invoke the version with known errors in earlier papers.
From FKS Lemma 2.1, Remark 2.2, Cor. 2.3 and Table 1
(PDF pp.4–5), two elementary bounds are
$$
2\sum_{0<\gamma \le T^*}1/\gamma \le y^2/6+3,\qquad
2\sum_{\beta>1/2,\,0<\gamma \le T^*}1/\gamma
\le (y^2-h^2)/12+.1.
$$
For the first use $U=100$, $S_0<.593$; for the second
use reflection at each positive ordinate, exclude ordinates
below $H$, and use $U=H$. In both cases the coefficient
in $2.1$ is $<1/6$, the remainder $2R(U)/U<.1$, and
the logarithm product is at most
$(y^2-(\log U)^2)/2$. The upper limit $e^y>T^*$ avoids
inclusive-endpoint issues.

def prelim():
    pi_check()
    for U0 in (I(100),I(H)):
        l=log(U0)
        r=I('.137')*l+I('.443')*log(l)+I('1.588')
        c=1/(2*PI)+(I('.137')*l+I('.443'))/(U0*l*log(U0/(2*PI)))
        assert c<I(F(1,6)) and 2*r/U0<I('.1')
    assert e(1)>I('2.45') and e(F(7,20)*t0)>max(51,t0)
    assert e(3*t0/20)>6 and e(t0/2)>2
    assert I(F(7,20)*t0+1)**2>2*h*h
    assert 4/t0 < b-s0 and 2/t0<b-F(1,2)
    assert I('18.42')>4
    assert (F(1,2)-a)>0
    assert I(F(19,100)*t0+1)>h and e(F(19,100)*t0)>t0
    assert (triangle(t0)+h*h/12)/I(t0)**2<I('.0034')
    c=F(27,100); Y=c*t0+log(I('2.45')); v=log(2*PI)
    assert Y>h
    # Since the additive shift in Y-v is negative, test 4/L using
    # the polynomial inequality 2[(Y-v)^2-(h-v)^2] >= cL(Y-v).
    o=log(I('2.45'))-v
    assert 2*((Y-v)**2-(h-v)**2)>c*t0*(Y-v)
    assert 2*c*t0+3*o>0 and c-a>1/t0
    assert e(c*t0)>t0 and e(t0/2)>2 and e((F(1,2)-c)*t0)>6

Split at $1/2$ and $s_*$ and use $|\rho|\ge|\gamma|$.
The **normalized** bound is
$$
 |e_{\psi}(L)|\le e^{-aL} C(L),\quad e_{\psi}(L)=e^{-L}\psi(e^L)-1,
\quad
 C=B_1(L)+[(y^2-h^2)/12+.1]e^{-(b-s_*)L}
 +(y^2/6+3)e^{-(b-1/2)L}+2.091Le^{-(c_*-a)L}.
$$
There is **no additional high-cutoff error** to add to this estimate:
the finite sum is already bounded by the unrestricted positive mass.
The coefficient is nonincreasing from 155 (for the quadratic log
factor subtracting $h^2$, the log derivative is $\le4/L$ since $y^2>2h^2$; the other quadratic has log derivative $\le2/L$).
The limit is $w_b$. Dusart Cor. 4.5 (PDF p.13) adds at most
$3e^{-L/2}$ to bound $|\theta(e^L)e^{-L}-1|$.
In the improved alternative, put $c_*=.27$ and
$y=c_*L+\log(2.45)$, use $B_1^\sharp$, and replace the
middle-strip reciprocal estimate by
$$
 \frac{(y-\log(2\pi))^2-(h-\log(2\pi))^2}{12}+.1.
$$
This retains the logarithm product in FKS (2.1) instead of
dropping its $2\pi$. For the inclusive sum we may first use
an upper log ordinate larger than $y$ and take its decreasing
limit. In the total reciprocal estimate use $y^2/6+3$ as
before. This alternative is also valid and nonincreasing from
155: for the middle polynomial, write $y-\log(2\pi)=c_*L+o$.
Its log derivative is at most $4/L$ because
$2[(c_*L+o)^2-(h-\log(2\pi))^2]>c_*L(c_*L+o)$ holds at
155 and the derivative of the difference is
$c_*(2c_*L+3o)>0$. The total-polynomial and truncation checks
are the same (use $c_*-a>1/155$). Both cutoff admissibility
conditions are checked from 155. In the applications at cap
$b$, $C$ denotes the minimum of the two valid curves; at cap
$7/8$ or for the Dusart-only shape use the stated unmodified
cutoff and licensed coefficients. Taking the minimum preserves
decrease and the limiting coefficient.

At $L=168$ the new absolute relative error is below
$A_0=\pi/(3\cdot10^{12})$. At $L=200$, $C<.215402$,
while the raw contract's scaled coefficient is 625 and increasing.
The exact test also gives $C<.213$ from 204; the current certificate does not give .213 at 200.
These gains use the cap inferred from A, rather than directly
inserting the much larger raw coefficient into the endpoint errors.

source_references.readback:
For the smoothed formulas let $J_1(L)=\int_L^\infty e_{\psi}(t)dt$.
Use the exact absolutely convergent formula derived in
`mertens_current.md`, §2, with residues as specified there:
$$
 J_1(L)=\sum_{\rho}\frac{e^{(\rho-1)L}}{\rho(\rho-1)}
        -\log(2\pi)e^{-L}+\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{e^{-(2k+1)L}}{2k(2k+1)} .
$$
The derivation uses the integrated Mellin kernel; it does not
interchange an unsmoothed conditional zero sum and integration.
Let $J_2$ be its termwise primitive with $J_2'=-J_1$;
this entails one more inverse $\rho-1$ in absolute value.
The trivial terms cost at most $2e^{-L}$ in each at the
arguments used. The line spectral weight is $<.04620$, by the
identity and exact gamma trim in the inherited proof (CH2 (B.9)
and `refine.py:test_M`); ordinates on the line exceed 14.
Using CH2 Cor. B.2 (PDF p.43) and partial summation,
$2\sum_{\gamma>H}1/\gamma^2<7\cdot10^{-12}$ (inclusion at
$H$ obeys the same integral upper bound). Thus on the
analytic Mertens domain $L\ge18.42$ put
$$
 j=.04620e^{-L/2}+2e^{-L}+e^{-aL}k,\qquad
 j_2=.04620e^{-L/2}/14+2e^{-L}+e^{-aL}k/H,
$$
with $k=7\cdot10^{-12}$ below 155 and, from 155, the minimum
of that constant and $B_2(L)+7\cdot10^{-12}e^{-(b-s_*)L}$.
Then $|J_1|\le j, |J_2|\le j_2$. In the high-strip bound
use $|\rho-1|\ge \gamma$, and off-line below $s_*$ use the
full reciprocal-square cap. These bounds only decrease, including
at the join. For the prime-count prefix at 20 use instead the
coarser $k=7\cdot10^{-12}$ everywhere (QRH-free alternative:
drop (e^{-aL}) from the off-line term). This is a second,
independent use of A's strip, including in signed Mertens bounds
below the unsmoothed handoff.

def smooth(L,alpha=a):
    x=I(L); B=1-alpha
    off=minI(I('7e-12'),scr2(L,B)) if L>=t0 else I('7e-12')
    j=I('.04620')*e(-(F(1,2)-alpha)*x)+2*e(-B*x)
    j2=I('.04620')/14*e(-(F(1,2)-alpha)*x)+2*e(-B*x)
    return j+off,j2+off/H

def test_M():
    n=1000
    Hn=sum(I(1)/k for k in range(1,n+1))
    gg=Hn-log(n)-I(1)/(2*n)+hull(0,F(1,n*n))
    assert 2+gg-log(4*PI)<I('.04620')

**An original-input boundary entry, independent of A.** There is
a slightly sharper pointwise alternative to CH2 Cor. 1.3 on
$x>H$: apply its Cor. 1.2 (PDF p.3, text line 201) at the full
verified height $T=H$ and bound $z\coth z-1\le z^2/3$ at
$z=\pi/H$. Write
$$
 A_H=\frac{\pi}{H-1}+\frac{(\pi/H)^2}{3},\qquad
 d_H=\frac{r^2-r/3}{2\pi},\qquad r=\log(H/(2\pi)).
$$
Then $|e_\psi(L)|\le A_H+d_He^{-L/2}$, and the absolute
centered $\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)/n$ error is at most
$\pi/(H-1)+d_He^{-L/2}$. Both are valid for real $x>H$
(strict domain of the source). Since $A_H<A_0$ and
$d_H<113.67$, they improve the respective Cor. 1.3
bounds everywhere on $x>H$. Insert them in the applicable
pointwise minima, including the weighted-sum boundary transfer;
the additive primitive and prime-power corrections are unchanged.
The tabulated compact bridges need only the slightly looser
$A_0$ curves. The high-ray comparisons with the CH2 floor
still hold with $A_H$ in place of $A_0$.

if __name__=='__main__':
    A_H=PI/(H-1)+(PI/H)**2/3
    v=log(H/(2*PI)); d_H=(v*v-v/3)/(2*PI)
    assert A_H<A0 and d_H<I('113.67')
    assert A_H*184**2>I('3.54e-8') and A_H*e(I(184)/8)>I('.01')
    assert I('.245')*e(-a*I(175))<A_H
    print('Original-input boundary constants A_H, d_H:',A_H,d_H,flush=True)

source_references.readback:
For $\Re s>1$, absolute convergence and unique factorization give
$$
-\zeta'(s)/\zeta(s)=s/(s-1)+s\int_1^\infty(\psi(t)-t)t^{-s-1}\,dt.
$$
The compact part before $e^{200}$ is harmless; the rest is normally
convergent on every compact subset of $\Re s>b$ by A. Thus the
right side continues holomorphically there except at 1. The identity
theorem and the nonzero residue of the logarithmic derivative at a zero
give $\beta \le b$ for each nontrivial zero. This is a **closed upper
cap**, not a proof of exclusion at $b$. The zeta continuation and
symmetries are the standard ones used in the allowed FKS §2 and CH2
Appendices A/B. No real zero in $0<s<1$ occurs: the alternating
Dirichlet series for $(1-2^{1-s})\zeta(s)$ is positive by pairing.
Count multiplicities throughout. This is why several improvements
start before $e^{200}$: the hypothesis controls an analytic
continuation globally; it is not directly evaluated below its threshold.

source_references.readback:
Let $H=3000175332800, h=\log H$. By Platt–Trudgian FiniteRH
Theorem 1 (original PDF p.2; announcement p.1), off-line zeros
of positive ordinate have ordinate at least $H$. Below we use
$H$ as a lower integration limit, so also allowing equality causes
no issue. Put $s_* =.72$. For $s\ge s_*$ in our screens let
$p=8(1-s)/3, q=5-2s$. Use the **first** FKS Table 8 panel
(PDF p.26, Cor. 2.9 and (2.17), pp.7–8) on its own interval, or
Dusart Theorem 2.3 (PDF p.5), to write a density bound
$$
N(s,t)\le c t^p(\log t)^q+d(\log t)^2\quad(t\ge H).
$$
FKS Remark 1.5(2), PDF p.3, explicitly distinguishes the
adopted .77 input from the announced .618 value (“if and when
… confirmed”). The latter is not imported or established from A here.
Use the stated interval corollary at original-paper trust, not a
new invocation of Thm. 2.7 with the separately displayed delta
parameter. For Dusart use $c=4.9\cdot3^p,d=51.5$ by $\log(1+v)\le v$.
Table constants are rounded **up** in `d02screen.py`; bounds are
minimized as whole bounds, not mixing coefficients. Changing the
integration limit does not change the $H_0=3\cdot10^{12}$ of the
FKS Table 8 parameters. The density results need not be reoptimized
at unmatched parameters. Whether an original includes $\beta=s$
does not matter; the cumulative mass below uses $\beta>s$.

For $m=1,2$ bound the two-sided mass
$2\sum_{\gamma>0, \beta>s}\gamma^{-m}$ by
$2m\int_H^\infty N(s,t)t^{-m-1}dt$. Put $\lambda=m-p>0,z=\lambda h$,
$$
A_z=\sum_{j=0}^3{3\choose j}j!/z^j,\qquad
B_z=\sum_{j=0}^3{3\choose j}(j+1)!/z^{j+1}.
$$
The bound per source is
$$
W_m(s;c,d)=
\frac{2mc e^{-z}h^q}{\lambda} A_z(1+B_z/A_z)^{q-3}
+2d e^{-mh}(h^2+2h/m+2/m^2).
$$
Indeed $t=H e^v$; with weight $e^{-\lambda v}(1+v/h)^3\,dv$,
the mean of $v/h$ is $B_z/A_z$. Concavity of
$(1+v/h)^{q-3}$ (here $3<q<4$) gives the displayed Jensen
upper bound. This also applies to the $m=2$ integral, instead of
merely dividing the $m=1$ bound by $H$.

Take nodes from $s_*$ to $b$ of step .00025. At each node below the
last one take the upward rounding of the min of the source values,
then the running minimum $w_j$ to preserve monotonicity. A preceding
upper bound for the tail is still valid later. For all but the last bin
use the left cumulative bound $w_j$; equivalently assign mass
$w_j-w_{j+1}$ at the right endpoint for estimating increasing
weights. For the last bin, from $s_{J-1}$ to $b$, use the
**linear chord** of the Dusart integral between its two upper endpoint
values $w_{J-1}$ and $w_b$. The checker verifies that at the left
it is indeed the selected upper value, and that it decreases. This
chord bounds the true Dusart majorant: each integrand in its first
term is a positive constant times an exponential of an affine
function of $s$ $because (p,q) are affine$; the second term is
constant. Hence the actual integrated majorant is convex. Avoid
an artificial atom of size $w_{J-1}-w_b$ at $b$: spread it
uniformly over this last bin, retaining $w_b$ at $b$.
Define $B_m(L)$ as the sum of the masses just specified times
$e^{-(b-s)L}$, with the uniform mass term integrated:
$$
 B_m(L)=\sum_{j<J-1}(w_j-w_{j+1})e^{-(b-s_{j+1})L}
 +w_b+(w_{J-1}-w_b)\frac{1-e^{-(b-s_{J-1})L}}{(b-s_{J-1})L}.
$$
This dominates the exponentially weighted actual mass by layer-cake
integration in $s$. At nodes any jump conventions in the auxiliary
majorant can be taken right-continuous; the true **strict** tail and
the value at $s_*$ are bounded. The $w_b$ term is an upper
allowance for a possible boundary atom, not an assertion it exists.
All terms are nonnegative and nonincreasing in $L$.
The chord is materially relevant to the limiting coefficient.
The limiting allowances satisfy $w_b<.116297$ for $m=1$ and
$w_b<2.506\cdot10^{-14}$ for $m=2$ (both strict). The same
routine with cap $7/8$ is an optional within-method B0 comparison,
not a replacement of any stronger inherited B0 branch.

**New multiple-chord majorant for $m=1$.**
At each regular bin $[s_j,s_{j+1})$, denote its two rounded
running-minimum endpoints by $w_j,w_{j+1}$. Whenever they
equal the upward-rounded Jensen estimates of the **same**
source with the same table block (for Dusart, same formula),
replace the constant tail majorant in the bin by the straight
line through these values. Convexity of the *exact moment
integral* of the chosen density bound proves this line is an
upper bound, whether or not the Jensen formula itself is
convex. Otherwise keep the old constant envelope with the
right-edge step. Equality of the rounded endpoints with a
particular source is checked by integer comparisons in
`chords()`; if any running min came from a previous node,
this rule is equally safe. At the cap keep the same last
Dusart chord and atom. The resulting decreasing tail gives
a positive measure supported in $[s_*,b]$, with weights
$w_j-w_{j+1}$ spread uniformly in selected bins and at the
right endpoints otherwise. Each of the selected uniform
contributions replaces $e^{-(b-r)L}$ at the right node $r$
by $e^{-(b-r)L}(1-e^{-(r-l)L})/[(r-l)L]$. The new
coefficient $B_1^\sharp$ is nonincreasing and no larger than
the old licensed $B_1$; they have the same terminal allowance.
The code uses a grouped Horner evaluation. The method bounds
the weighted **strict** zero tail on the entire strip by layer
integration; it neither assumes zero-free table joins nor removes
possible zeros at the cap. We continue to use the original
licensed $B_2$ for smoothing.

Let $T=e^{c_*L}$ with $c_*=7/20$, $y=c_*L+1$. From $L=155$
use FKS Thm. 3.2 (PDF p.8) with the row
$(\log x_M,\alpha,\omega,M)=(40,1/2,0,2.091)$.
The two admissibility inequalities $T>\max(51,L)$ and
$5T+2<e^{L/2}$ hold at 155 and persist (the ratios of
the exponential to each competing term increase).
The formula gives a possibly different $T^*$ at every
argument; $T\le T^*\le2.45T<e^y$. No prime-power midpoint
convention is substituted for this original signed formula
on its real domain. See FKS Remark 3.3 for the stated provenance;
we do not invoke the version with known errors in earlier papers.
From FKS Lemma 2.1, Remark 2.2, Cor. 2.3 and Table 1
(PDF pp.4–5), two elementary bounds are
$$
2\sum_{0<\gamma \le T^*}1/\gamma \le y^2/6+3,\qquad
2\sum_{\beta>1/2,\,0<\gamma \le T^*}1/\gamma
\le (y^2-h^2)/12+.1.
$$
For the first use $U=100$, $S_0<.593$; for the second
use reflection at each positive ordinate, exclude ordinates
below $H$, and use $U=H$. In both cases the coefficient
in $2.1$ is $<1/6$, the remainder $2R(U)/U<.1$, and
the logarithm product is at most
$(y^2-(\log U)^2)/2$. The upper limit $e^y>T^*$ avoids
inclusive-endpoint issues.

def prelim():
    pi_check()
    for U0 in (I(100),I(H)):
        l=log(U0)
        r=I('.137')*l+I('.443')*log(l)+I('1.588')
        c=1/(2*PI)+(I('.137')*l+I('.443'))/(U0*l*log(U0/(2*PI)))
        assert c<I(F(1,6)) and 2*r/U0<I('.1')
    assert e(1)>I('2.45') and e(F(7,20)*t0)>max(51,t0)
    assert e(3*t0/20)>6 and e(t0/2)>2
    assert I(F(7,20)*t0+1)**2>2*h*h
    assert 4/t0 < b-s0 and 2/t0<b-F(1,2)
    assert I('18.42')>4
    assert (F(1,2)-a)>0
    assert I(F(19,100)*t0+1)>h and e(F(19,100)*t0)>t0
    assert (triangle(t0)+h*h/12)/I(t0)**2<I('.0034')
    c=F(27,100); Y=c*t0+log(I('2.45')); v=log(2*PI)
    assert Y>h
    # Since the additive shift in Y-v is negative, test 4/L using
    # the polynomial inequality 2[(Y-v)^2-(h-v)^2] >= cL(Y-v).
    o=log(I('2.45'))-v
    assert 2*((Y-v)**2-(h-v)**2)>c*t0*(Y-v)
    assert 2*c*t0+3*o>0 and c-a>1/t0
    assert e(c*t0)>t0 and e(t0/2)>2 and e((F(1,2)-c)*t0)>6

Split at $1/2$ and $s_*$ and use $|\rho|\ge|\gamma|$.
The **normalized** bound is
$$
 |e_{\psi}(L)|\le e^{-aL} C(L),\quad e_{\psi}(L)=e^{-L}\psi(e^L)-1,
\quad
 C=B_1(L)+[(y^2-h^2)/12+.1]e^{-(b-s_*)L}
 +(y^2/6+3)e^{-(b-1/2)L}+2.091Le^{-(c_*-a)L}.
$$
There is **no additional high-cutoff error** to add to this estimate:
the finite sum is already bounded by the unrestricted positive mass.
The coefficient is nonincreasing from 155 (for the quadratic log
factor subtracting $h^2$, the log derivative is $\le4/L$ since $y^2>2h^2$; the other quadratic has log derivative $\le2/L$).
The limit is $w_b$. Dusart Cor. 4.5 (PDF p.13) adds at most
$3e^{-L/2}$ to bound $|\theta(e^L)e^{-L}-1|$.
In the improved alternative, put $c_*=.27$ and
$y=c_*L+\log(2.45)$, use $B_1^\sharp$, and replace the
middle-strip reciprocal estimate by
$$
 \frac{(y-\log(2\pi))^2-(h-\log(2\pi))^2}{12}+.1.
$$
This retains the logarithm product in FKS (2.1) instead of
dropping its $2\pi$. For the inclusive sum we may first use
an upper log ordinate larger than $y$ and take its decreasing
limit. In the total reciprocal estimate use $y^2/6+3$ as
before. This alternative is also valid and nonincreasing from
155: for the middle polynomial, write $y-\log(2\pi)=c_*L+o$.
Its log derivative is at most $4/L$ because
$2[(c_*L+o)^2-(h-\log(2\pi))^2]>c_*L(c_*L+o)$ holds at
155 and the derivative of the difference is
$c_*(2c_*L+3o)>0$. The total-polynomial and truncation checks
are the same (use $c_*-a>1/155$). Both cutoff admissibility
conditions are checked from 155. In the applications at cap

For the smoothed formulas let $J_1(L)=\int_L^\infty e_{\psi}(t)dt$.
Use the exact absolutely convergent formula derived in
`mertens_current.md`, §2, with residues as specified there:
$$
 J_1(L)=\sum_{\rho}\frac{e^{(\rho-1)L}}{\rho(\rho-1)}
        -\log(2\pi)e^{-L}+\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{e^{-(2k+1)L}}{2k(2k+1)} .
$$
The derivation uses the integrated Mellin kernel; it does not
interchange an unsmoothed conditional zero sum and integration.
Let $J_2$ be its termwise primitive with $J_2'=-J_1$;
this entails one more inverse $\rho-1$ in absolute value.
The trivial terms cost at most $2e^{-L}$ in each at the
arguments used. The line spectral weight is $<.04620$, by the
identity and exact gamma trim in the inherited proof (CH2 (B.9)
and `refine.py:test_M`); ordinates on the line exceed 14.
Using CH2 Cor. B.2 (PDF p.43) and partial summation,
$2\sum_{\gamma>H}1/\gamma^2<7\cdot10^{-12}$ (inclusion at
$H$ obeys the same integral upper bound). Thus on the
analytic Mertens domain $L\ge18.42$ put
$$
 j=.04620e^{-L/2}+2e^{-L}+e^{-aL}k,\qquad
 j_2=.04620e^{-L/2}/14+2e^{-L}+e^{-aL}k/H,
$$
with $k=7\cdot10^{-12}$ below 155 and, from 155, the minimum
of that constant and $B_2(L)+7\cdot10^{-12}e^{-(b-s_*)L}$.
Then $|J_1|\le j, |J_2|\le j_2$. In the high-strip bound
use $|\rho-1|\ge \gamma$, and off-line below $s_*$ use the
full reciprocal-square cap. These bounds only decrease, including
at the join. For the prime-count prefix at 20 use instead the
coarser $k=7\cdot10^{-12}$ everywhere (QRH-free alternative:
drop (e^{-aL}) from the off-line term). This is a second,
independent use of A's strip, including in signed Mertens bounds
below the unsmoothed handoff.

    x=I(L); B=1-alpha
    off=minI(I('7e-12'),scr2(L,B)) if L>=t0 else I('7e-12')

    j2=I('.04620')/14*e(-(F(1,2)-alpha)*x)+2*e(-B*x)
    return j+off,j2+off/H

this covers every real $x\ge38358837683$ up to the analytic
overlap. A quotient sieve independently checks both counts on
the first unit, including the possible $x/e$ jumps.

def primecount(n):
    if n<2:
        return 0
    r=isqrt(n)
    vs=[n//i for i in range(1,r+1)]
    vs+=list(range(vs[-1]-1,0,-1))
    s={v:v-1 for v in vs}
    for p in range(2,r+1):
        if s[p]==s[p-1]:
            continue
        sp=s[p-1]
        pp=p*p
        for v in vs:
            if v<pp: break
            s[v]-=s[v//p]-sp
    return s[n]

def main():
    # Independent small input checks against an elementary Eratosthenes sieve.
    sv=sieve(500)
    assert all(primecount(n)==sum(sv[:n+1]) for n in range(501))
    N=38358837682
    M=14111427770
    assert (N+1)%2521==0 and 1<2521<N+1
    el,eu=ei(F(1))
    assert M*eu<N<=N+1<(M+1)*el
    P,Q=primecount(N),primecount(M)
    assert (P,Q)==(1644673232,632207037)
    def gap(x):
        l,u=lu(x)
        return el*x*Q/u-P*P,eu*x*Q/l-P*P

    # and lie in the same no-jump cell of both pi factors.
    l=N+F('0.21792636514465772878')
    r=N+F('0.21792636514465772879')
    assert gap(l)[1]<0<gap(r)[0]
    assert gap(N+F(1,10))[1]<0<gap(N+1)[0]
    Ll,_=lu(N)
    _,Lu=lu(N+1)
    assert 67_000_000<el*Q*(Ll-1)/Lu**2
    assert eu*Q*(Lu-1)/Ll**2<68_000_000
    print(P,Q,str(l),str(r),flush=True)

def strengthened_tail(L,n,N,k=0,B=b,kind=None):
    x=I(L)
    assert F(k)<=ac(n) # the retained tail polynomial has nonnegative coefficients
    if kind is None:
        assert L>=t0+1 and L>N/(1-B)+3
        err=loss(L,L,n,N,B,True)
    else:
        assert L>=201 and L>n/(1-b)+20
        d1,d2=kind(L-1),kind(L)
        pp,v=uu(L,N)
        err=x**n*(x/(x-1)*d1+(2*(pp+v)+d2)*d2)
    return polyr(L,n,N)-I(k)-err-qerr(L,L,n,N)

def high_table():
    for n in range(7,41):
        N=max(17,n+5)
        def first(B):
            l=max(int(N/(1-B))+4,156); r=47*n
            assert strengthened_tail(r,n,N,B=B)>0
            while r-l>1:
                j=(l+r)//2
                if strengthened_tail(j,n,N,B=B)>0:r=j
                else:l=j
            assert strengthened_tail(r,n,N,B=B)>0
            assert strengthened_tail(r-1,n,N,B=B)<0
            return r
        aa,bb=first(b),first(F(7,8))
        alt=polyr(aa,n,N)-loss(aa,aa,n,N,F(7,8))-qerr(aa,aa,n,N)
        assert aa<bb and alt<0
        print(n-4,N,aa,bb,'fraction of next coefficient left:',strengthened_tail(aa,n,N)/ac(n), flush=True)

def strengthened_tail(L,n,N,k=0,B=b,kind=None):
    x=I(L)
    assert F(k)<=ac(n) # the retained tail polynomial has nonnegative coefficients
    if kind is None:
        assert L>=t0+1 and L>N/(1-B)+3
        err=loss(L,L,n,N,B,True)
    else:
        assert L>=201 and L>n/(1-b)+20
        d1,d2=kind(L-1),kind(L)
        pp,v=uu(L,N)
        err=x**n*(x/(x-1)*d1+(2*(pp+v)+d2)*d2)
    return polyr(L,n,N)-I(k)-err-qerr(L,L,n,N)

for the shifted argument inferred at $x$.

$$

 &+3.04620e^{-t/2}/(.4t)+7\cdot10^{-12}e^{-at}/[(b-.1)t]

`ramanujan.md` §2, entry 6, gives this bound: anchor at $d$
(the normalized residual after removing the theta boundary
is at most (3d e^{10-d})); integrate $-J_1'$ against

negative integral before 10, the initial smoothed endpoint, and
the possibly negative PV normalization is $<241$:
split the preintegral at $\log100$ and bound the denominators
by $(2/3)^2$, $(\log100)^2$, respectively, and use up to 4
for the normalization. From 10 to 20 use
$(e^{\lambda v}/v^2)'\ge(\lambda-.2)e^{\lambda v}/v^2$;
from 20 onward use (lambda-.1). Set $g=1.046200147$.

$$
\begin{split}
 D_{\rm low}^-(t)={}&1.751000147e^{-t/2}+1.78e^{-2t/3}+j_0(t)/t\\

             +\frac{1.78e^{20/3}}{400(1/3-.2)}\right)t e^{-t}\\

 +\frac{1.78 e^{-2t/3}}{(1/3-.1)t}

\end{split}
$$

For integer $N\ge17$ in the finite certificates, put
$P_N(t)=\sum_{j=0}^N j!/t^j$ and
$f_N(t)=\sum_{j=0}^N(1-j/t)^{-1}$ for $t>N+1$.
Use
$$
P_N(t)-f_N(t)e^{1-t} < F(t) < P_N(t)+d_N(t)
$$
with
$$
d_N(t)=4t e^{-t}+
\min\big((N+1)!/t^N, 2(N+1)!/t^{N+1}+t e^{-t/2}\big).
$$
To verify, substitute $v=t-\log u$ in $\int_e^{e^t}du/\log u$.
The finite geometric sum through degree $N$ has positive
remainder $(v/t)^{N+1}/(1-v/t)$. Its integral over
$0\le v\le t-1$ can be bounded by $t$ times the full
moment, or by splitting at $t/2$ and bounding the two
pieces with 2 and $t$ respectively. Missing moment
tails are bounded using $(1+w/t)^j\le e^{jw/t}$ after
$v=t-1+w$. Also $0<\operatorname{li}(e)<4$.
This accounts for the direction of both errors.

Expand $L P_N(L-1)/(L-1)$ in powers of $1/L$ with
positive binomial coefficients. Through degree $N$ the
difference from $P_N(L)^2$ has coefficients $a_n$.
For $n\ge6$, $a_n/n!\ge 65/24-(2+4/n)>1/24$:
bound the two end binomial reciprocals by 1 each, the
next two by $1/n$, and all other $n-3$ entries by
$2/[n(n-1)]$; lower bound the factorial reciprocal sum
through degree 4. Directly check the small $a_n$.
The sign argument applies also at degrees beyond the
computational tables.

source_references.readback:
The checker subtracts the positive tails explicitly. In
unnormalized units for $G/L^4$, define the main error allowance
$$
 E_N=(2P_N+d_N)d_N+\frac{L}{L-1} f_N(L-1)e^{2-L}
 +\sum_{0\le j,k\le N, j+k>N}\frac{j!k!}{L^{j+k}} .
$$
The count-error allowance is
$$
 E_{\pi}=\frac{L}{L-1}D_-(L-1)+(2[P_N(L)+d_N(L)]+D_+(L))D_+(L).
$$
Thus $G(L)>\sum_{j=4}^N a_j/L^{j-4}-L^4(E_N+E_\pi)$.
For a profile missing the term of degree $n$ first,
the lower reserve at scale $L^{n-4}$ uses powers
$a_j/L^{j-n}$, $j=n,\ldots,N$.
On a closed cell $[l,r]$ every nonnegative decreasing
error factor is bounded at $l$, and the multiplying power
$L^n$ and lower polynomial at $r$. Domain-dependent bounds
are used only when they hold on the whole argument interval.
In particular at $x/e$ the bounds are selected with
$[l-1,r-1]$, not just the starting argument.

For the integer-log tail table and the fixed $K$ tails a
stronger single-check argument **keeps all the excess main
coefficients**: after multiplying by $L^N$, the reserve
polynomial is nondecreasing, since all coefficients of the
remaining $a_j$ (or $a_6-K$) are nonnegative. The scaled
total errors decrease on the tail: powers of $1/L$ and
other rational prefactors decrease; $L^N e^{-c(L-h)}$
decreases for $L>N/c$, and with an extra factor $(L-h)^i$
use $N/L+i/(L-h)<c$. For the screened error factor use the
monotone $C$ and $c=a$ or $1/8$ (no growing positive
power multiplies that term except $L^N$); standalone
terms with $i=1$ have faster decay. These inequalities
hold at every checked tail. The direct-A variant has $i\le2$
at rate $a$ and starts its tail at 222. In $E_N$, the slowest
pure inverse power of the remainder has degree $N$, and
the fastest scale of the exponential factors is $L^{N+1}$
at decay at least $1/2$. The minimum of the two remainder
branches after positive scaling is nonincreasing. This proves
every infinite tail rather than extrapolating the samples.

def main():
    prelim()
    T=F('167.84')
    assert combined(F(155)) < I('.3')
    # Independent-of-A shortcut to the first q=2 bridge row.
    z2=lambda t:bz(t)+(I('7e-12')*e(-I(t)/8))*(1+1/I(t)+2*(1/I(t)+2/I(t)**2)/H)
    left=F('59.5'); right=F(188)
    assert maxI(z2(left)*I(left)**2,z2(right)*I(right)**2)/(1-z2(left)/I(left))<I('5.30e-8')
    import portfolio_check as old
    assert I(old.spectral(right).U())<I('.014')
    x=I(right); J=I('.04620')*e(-x/2)+2*e(-x)+I('7e-12')*e(-x/8)
    B=I('.014')*e(-x/8)+ (1+1/x)*J+2*(1/x+2/x**2)*J+2*e(-x/2)+x*e(-x)
    assert x*x*B/(1-B/x)<I('5.30e-8')
    rows=[('59.5',0,2,'5.30e-8'),('60.98',0,2,'2.951e-8'),('59.5',0,3,'4.952e-6'),
          ('59.5',0,4,'.0008311'),('59.5',0,5,'.13950'),('59.5',0,6,'23.412'),
          ('59.5',F(1,8),0,'.001354'),('59.5',F(9,64),0,'.018643'),('59.5',a,0,'.256707')]
    for L,al,q,c in rows:
        v=convexbridge(F(L),T,al,q)
        assert q<=(a-al)*T
        v=maxI(v,combined(T)*I(T)**q*e((al-a)*I(T)))
        assert v<I(c),(L,al,q,c,v)
        print('bridge (L, alpha, q), combined upper cap',L,al,q,v,flush=True)
    levels=[(168,'.256418'),(170,'.252899'),(175,'.244823'),(180,'.237637'),
                (190,'.225412'),(200,'.215402'),(225,'.196863'),
                (250,'.184130'),(300,'.167809'),(400,'.151060'),
                (600,'.137363'),(1000,'.129304')]
    more=[(173,'.248838'),(175,'.245767'),(181,'.238698'),(185,'.232384'),
          (195,'.221577'),(205,'.212654'),(228,'.195899'),
          (204,'.213'),(180,'.239'),(1000,'.128081')]
    for L,c in levels+more:
        v=combined(F(L));assert v<I(c),(L,v,c)
        print('D02 power ray, L and bound',L,c,v,flush=True)
    for L,c in [(168,'.261492'),(175,'.249146'),(180,'.241556'),(200,'.218341'),(250,'.186256')]:
        assert spec(F(L),dusart_only=True)<I(c)
    for l,al,q,c in [('168',0,2,'2.944e-8'),('168',0,3,'4.935e-6'),
                     ('168',0,4,'.0008274'),('168',0,5,'.13872'),('168',0,6,'23.257'),
                     ('169',F(1,8),0,'.001323'),('171',F(9,64),0,'.018165'),
                     ('173',a,0,'.249412')]:
        assert q<=(a-al)*F(l)
        v=combined(F(l))*I(l)**q*e((al-a)*I(l))
        assert v<I(c),(l,al,q,c,v)
        print('fixed-target later ray',l,al,q,v,flush=True)
    finitejoins()
    tape=Path('repair_tape.txt').read_text()
    base=Path('d02finite_results.txt').read_text()
    p,q=tape.split('New shape:'); u,v=q.split('k/100')
    pp,qq=base.split('New shape:'); uu,vv=qq.split('k/100')
    assert p==pp and v==vv
    rows=lambda z:dict((int(k),tuple(map(int,v.split()))) for k,v in
                           (ln.split(':') for ln in z.splitlines()[1:]))
    new,prior=rows(u),rows(uu)
    assert all(new[k]==prior[k] for k in prior)
    for k in sorted(set(new)-set(prior)):
        assert k>=1354 and all(75000000<=t<250000000 for t in new[k])
        print('new finite tape: coefficient units 1e-6, (P/Q,S,V)',k,new[k],flush=True)

    rows=[('59.5',0,2,'5.30e-8'),('60.98',0,2,'2.951e-8'),('59.5',0,3,'4.952e-6'),

def combined(L,B=b):
    x=I(L); alpha=1-B
    J,J2=smooth(L,alpha)
    Y=(F(27,100) if B==b else F(7,20))*x
    v=screen(L,B,c=F(7,20))+2*(Y+1)*e(-Y)/PI+2*e(-B*x)
    z=v+J/x+2*(1/x+2/x**2)*J2+2*e(-(F(1,2)-alpha)*x)+x*e(-B*x)
    return z/(1-z*e(-alpha*x)/x)

For example, one may start **all** log powers $q\ge6$
already at $L=59.5$: put $T_0=167.84$, $v=\max(T_0,q/a)$.
A strict coefficient in $\mathcal E<c/L^q$ is
$$
 c=23.412\, T_0^{q-6}\,(v/T_0)^q e^{-a(v-T_0)} .
$$
On the bridge multiply the $q=6$ bound by at most $T_0^{q-6}$;
the extra factor is at least one. On the tail use $Z(L)\le
Z(T_0)$ and the exact maximum of $L^q e^{-aL}$ at $v$, together
with the strict $q=6$ tail check at $T_0$. These higher powers
are reweightings of one proof.

Let $P=\prod_{p\le x}(1-1/p), Q=1/P$ and use the real
convention $p\le x$. Write
$$
 \delta_Q=\log Q-\gamma-\log L,\quad
 \delta_S=\sum_{p\le x}1/p-\log L-M,\quad
 \delta_V=\sum_{p\le x}(\log p)/p-L+B_3 .
$$
Here $M=\gamma+\sum_p[\log(1-1/p)+1/p]$ and
$B_3=\gamma+\sum_p(\log p)/(p(p-1))$, exactly as in
Dusart Thms. 5.6–5.7 (PDF pp.17–18). Define the common error
quantity
$$
 \mathcal E(x)=\max\{L|e^{-\delta_Q}-1|, L|e^{\delta_Q}-1|,
                            L|\delta_S|, |\delta_V|\}.
$$
The two signed product factors are $e^{-\delta_Q}$ and
$e^{\delta_Q}$; the maximum of the two unscaled relative
errors is exactly $e^{|\delta_Q|}-1$.

def combined(L,B=b):
    x=I(L); alpha=1-B
    J,J2=smooth(L,alpha)
    Y=(F(27,100) if B==b else F(7,20))*x
    v=screen(L,B,c=F(7,20))+2*(Y+1)*e(-Y)/PI+2*e(-B*x)
    z=v+J/x+2*(1/x+2/x**2)*J2+2*e(-(F(1,2)-alpha)*x)+x*e(-B*x)
    return z/(1-z*e(-alpha*x)/x)

## 1. Exact identities and signed refinement at every point

Let $K(v)=(1+v)/v^2$, $D_1=\sum_{p^k>x,k\ge2}\log p/p^k$,
$D_0=\sum_{p^k>x,k\ge2}1/(kp^k)$,
$\tau=\sum_{p>x,k\ge2}1/(kp^k)$, and $D_Q=D_0-\tau$.
The exact real identities, including at jumps, are
$$
 \delta_V=e_{\psi}(L)-J_1(L)+D_1,\quad
 \delta_S=e_{\psi}(L)/L-\int_L^\infty e_{\psi}(v)K(v)dv+D_0,\quad
 \delta_Q=\delta_S-\tau .
$$
They follow by Abel summation of
$\sum\Lambda(n)/n$ and $\sum\Lambda(n)/(n\log n)$,
subtracting constants at infinity and adding the omitted prime
powers; details in `mertens_current.md` §2. For example the
normalization $M$ identifies the $U_0$ limit as $\gamma$
because the full correction beyond all prime powers is absolutely
summable, and the $U_1$ limit is $-B_3+(B_3-\gamma)$.
No equality assumes the RH. The same method from $\theta$
instead of $\psi$ gives the alternative direct signed
integral envelope in `mertens_current.md` §4, also allowing
the D02 theta curve under the integral.

def combined(L,B=b):
    x=I(L); alpha=1-B
    J,J2=smooth(L,alpha)
    Y=(F(27,100) if B==b else F(7,20))*x
    v=screen(L,B,c=F(7,20))+2*(Y+1)*e(-Y)/PI+2*e(-B*x)
    z=v+J/x+2*(1/x+2/x**2)*J2+2*e(-(F(1,2)-alpha)*x)+x*e(-B*x)
    return z/(1-z*e(-alpha*x)/x)

source_references.readback:
By two integrations by parts and $J_2'=-J_1$,
$$
 J_K(L)=K(L)j(L)+2|K'(L)|j_2(L)
        \ge  \left|\int_L^\infty e_{\psi}(v)K(v)dv\right|.
$$
Indeed the integral is $K(L)J_1(L)+\int_L^\infty J_1K'$;
the last integral is $J_2(L)K'(L)+\int_L^\infty J_2K''$.
Here $K''>0$ and $\int_L^\infty K''=|K'(L)|$.
All boundary limits hold by boundedness of the primitives.
Use $j,j_2$ of D02.md §3. This improves the simple
inherited smoothed off-line factor $e^{-L/8}$ on the
**whole** domain $L\ge18.42$, even when the boundary
$\psi(x)$ is not improved by A. The conditional exponent
is applied to an absolutely convergent series, not to an
uncertified extrapolation of a finite tail. A known boundary
value $e_{\psi}(L)$ can be kept exactly, with a strict-tail
correction interval rather than replacing it by a worst-case error.

def smooth(L,alpha=a):
    x=I(L); B=1-alpha
    off=minI(I('7e-12'),scr2(L,B)) if L>=t0 else I('7e-12')
    j=I('.04620')*e(-(F(1,2)-alpha)*x)+2*e(-B*x)
    j2=I('.04620')/14*e(-(F(1,2)-alpha)*x)+2*e(-B*x)
    return j+off,j2+off/H

For $L\ge18.42$, choose both signs of $e_{\psi}(L)$ as in
`mertens_current.md` §2, taking their separate minima
also with $e^{-aL}C(L)$ when $L\ge155$ and with the
contract on its actual direct domain. Call the signed
interval $[-E_-,E_+]$. For $\delta_V$ add the $D_1$
interval to $[-E_- - j,E_++j]$; for $\delta_S,\delta_Q$
add the $D_0,D_Q$ intervals to
$[-E_-/L-J_K,E_+/L+J_K]$.
The $D_i$ intervals in that section apply unchanged
($0\le D_1\le2e^{-L/2}, 0\le D_Q\le D_0\le2 e^{-L/2}/L$
are sufficient over the high bridge). For a certified
$[l,u]$ for $\delta_Q$, the product intervals are
$[e^l,e^u]$ for $Q$'s normalized factor and
$[e^{-u},e^{-l}]$ for $P$'s. Take the best separate
endpoints, not only the common-error tables. The finite
product and signed prime-sum branches retain their own
better endpoints where applicable.

def lowcover(lo,hi,step,alpha,q):
    x,hi,step=F(lo),F(hi),F(step)
    worst=I(0)
    while x<hi:
        y=min(x+step,hi)
        mode=0 if y<=F('29.9') else 1 if y<=F('43.7') else 2
        assert not any(x<t<y for t in [F('29.9'),F('43.7')])
        v=I(d01scale(x,y,mode,plain=True).U())*I(y)**q*e(I(y)*alpha)
        worst=maxI(worst,v)
        x=y
    return worst

For each $k=2,3$ take $y=x^{1/k}$,
$f(t)=t^{-k}$ for $D_1$, and $f(t)=1/(kt^k\log t)$
for $D_0$; the latter integral is
$\frac1k\int_{(1-1/k)L}^\infty e^{-w}dw/w$.
For $\tau$ take $y=x$ and $k=2,3$ in the latter kernel.
Use $d(y)=A_0+117/\sqrt y$ or, where applicable, any
decreasing majorant from D02.md §3 and the inherited profiles,
and intersect the resulting intervals.
For the unsummed $k\ge4$ part of $D_1$, upper-bound by
$$
 \frac{2e^{-3L/4}}{\log 2}
       \left(\frac{4L}{3}+\frac{16}{9}\right).
$$
In fact $\sum_{4\le k\le v/\log2}\theta(e^{v/k})
\le2(v/\log2)e^{v/4}$ by Dusart Thm. 4.2 $(k=0)$,
and dropping the negative boundary in Abel summation gives
the integral of this bound times $e^{-v}$.
Divide by $L$ for $D_0$ or as a subset bound for $\tau$.
For $\tau$ the even smaller elementary bound for $k\ge4$
is $\sum_{n>\lfloor x\rfloor}1/[4n^3(n-1)]$.
Use zero as lower bound for these remaining positive tails.
These corrections improve directional accuracy independently
of the main spectral term. D02 enters them only when the
theta bound at the relevant *root* is improved, not by using
the unrooted onset improperly.

source_references.readback:
There is a slightly stronger symmetric spectral bound than
adding $C e^{-aL}$ and the absolute integral independently.
With $T=e^{c_* L}$ (either licensed cutoff in D02.md), the $|\gamma|\le T^*$ terms of
$e_{\psi}-J_1$ from the two formulas in D02.md combine **exactly**
to $-e^{(\rho-1)L}/(\rho-1)$. Its absolute denominator
is still at least $|\gamma|$, so the *same* screen bounds
the sum. Only the smoothed high tail, not the unsmoothed
one, must be added. By CH2 Cor. B.2 and the $\beta \le b$
cap its relative size is at most $e^{-aL}\eta(L)$ with
$\eta(L)=2(c_*L+1)e^{-c_*L}/\pi$ (integrate the count over
$t\ge T$ against $4/t^3$ and drop $-\log(2\pi)$).
The trivial terms in $J_1$ add at most $2e^{-L}$, and the
FKS truncation term has already been paid in $C$.
For the minimum screen at cap $b$ use $c_*=.27$ in $\eta$
regardless of which branch attained the minimum: its tail
allowance is at least the one for .35. Put $U=C+\eta+2e^{-bL}$ and $J=e^{aL}j, J'=e^{aL}j_2$
(the prime on this last symbol is just a label).
Then $|\delta_V-D_1|\le e^{-aL}U$, and each of
$|\delta_S-D_0|, |\delta_Q-D_Q|$ is bounded by
$$
 \frac{e^{-aL}}{L}
 \left[U+\frac{J}{L}+2(1/L+2/L^2)J'\right].
$$
For the latter subtract $e_{\psi}-J_1$ from $e_{\psi}-L\int e_{\psi} K$;
the remaining terms are $-J_1/L-L\int J_1K'$, as bounded above.
This joint bound and the separate signed intervals need not
dominate each other for every endpoint. Retain their intersection.

One convenient common ray uses
$$
 z=U+J/L+2(1/L+2/L^2)J' +2e^{-(1/2-a)L}+Le^{-bL},\qquad
 Z=\frac{z}{1-ze^{-aL}/L}.
$$
Then $\mathcal E(x)\le e^{-aL}Z(L)$ for $L\ge155$.
The last positive term is optional (it upper-allows the
$\tau$ correction even when the tight $D_Q$ interval
isn't used). The prime-power bounds suffice on this entire
domain. The denominator is positive at 155, and the
individual $z$-terms and $e^{-aL}/L$ decrease; the
bound follows from $e^v-1\le v/(1-v)$ for $0\le v<1$.
This proves the limiting allowance $w_b<.116297$, without
even the residual reciprocal-square coefficient from the
separate summands. The no-FKS-table alternative in the table
uses the easier separate bounds, with the unrefined $k$
and $J'\le J$.

Between $59.5$ and $T_0=167.84$ use CH2 Cor. 1.3
(PDF p.3) at the boundary and $j_c$, $j_{c,2}$ in the
integral (the unrefined $k=7\cdot10^{-12}$).
An unscaled common numerator is
$$
 B(L)=A_0+115.67\,e^{-L/2}+(1+1/L)j_c(L)
   +2(1/L+2/L^2)j_{c,2}(L)+Le^{-L}.
$$
Here $115.67=113.67+2$; $j_c,j_{c,2}$ have the line and
trivial terms and the unrefined off-line weights of D02.md.
Then $\mathcal E\le B(L)/(1-B(L)/L)$.
For every power shape in the tables, $L^q e^{\alpha L}B(L)$
is convex on the compact bridge at the listed $(q,\alpha)$. For terms $L^d e^{-cL}$,
when $d\ge1$ and $c>0$ use
$L^2 f''/f=(cL-d)^2-d\ge0$ for $cL\ge d+\sqrt d$;
when $d\le0, c\ge0$, the differentiated terms are
nonnegative. The $A_0 L^q e^{\alpha L}$ term is convex
for the tested exponents $q=0$ or $q\ge2$.
For the least off-line decay at $q>0$ use
$(6+\sqrt6)/a<59.5$, and for the additional degree
from $Le^{-L}$ use its faster decay. Thus only the
**two ends** are needed for the numerator maximum, and
the conversion denominator is smallest at the left end.
For $L\ge T_0$, the tail multiplier $L^q e^{(\alpha-a)L}$
is nonincreasing in each tested case, as is $Z(L)$.
Checking the closed join on both sides certifies all rays,
including the tails. This is not an inference from a sampled graph.
For the $5.30\cdot10^{-8}$ row alone with B0, use $L^2 B(L)$
with off-line rate $1/8$ on $[59.5,188]$; its convex
maximum is still at 59.5 (or bound both by $5.30\cdot10^{-8}$).
From 188 use the inherited B0 spectral branch, whose
$L^2$-scaled ceiling is $<5.30\cdot10^{-8}$ there and decreases.

def main():
    prelim()
    T=F('167.84')
    assert combined(F(155)) < I('.3')
    # Independent-of-A shortcut to the first q=2 bridge row.
    z2=lambda t:bz(t)+(I('7e-12')*e(-I(t)/8))*(1+1/I(t)+2*(1/I(t)+2/I(t)**2)/H)
    left=F('59.5'); right=F(188)
    assert maxI(z2(left)*I(left)**2,z2(right)*I(right)**2)/(1-z2(left)/I(left))<I('5.30e-8')
    import portfolio_check as old
    assert I(old.spectral(right).U())<I('.014')
    x=I(right); J=I('.04620')*e(-x/2)+2*e(-x)+I('7e-12')*e(-x/8)
    B=I('.014')*e(-x/8)+ (1+1/x)*J+2*(1/x+2/x**2)*J+2*e(-x/2)+x*e(-x)
    assert x*x*B/(1-B/x)<I('5.30e-8')
    rows=[('59.5',0,2,'5.30e-8'),('60.98',0,2,'2.951e-8'),('59.5',0,3,'4.952e-6'),
          ('59.5',0,4,'.0008311'),('59.5',0,5,'.13950'),('59.5',0,6,'23.412'),
          ('59.5',F(1,8),0,'.001354'),('59.5',F(9,64),0,'.018643'),('59.5',a,0,'.256707')]
    for L,al,q,c in rows:
        v=convexbridge(F(L),T,al,q)
        assert q<=(a-al)*T
        v=maxI(v,combined(T)*I(T)**q*e((al-a)*I(T)))
        assert v<I(c),(L,al,q,c,v)
        print('bridge (L, alpha, q), combined upper cap',L,al,q,v,flush=True)

**Finite joins for the three power shapes.** For $9/64,5/32$
the script reweights each inherited finite26 band's certified
ceiling $c_b/L^2$ for $\mathcal E$, from 300000 to $10^8$.
The maximum of $e^{\alpha L}/L^2$ on a band is at an endpoint
(its sole interior stationary point is a minimum).
The inherited signed analytic branch is rechecked in closed
log cells on $[18.42,29.9],[29.9,43.7],[43.7,59.5]$,
using the QRH-free smoothed term for these low intervals.
Every cell uses a true enclosure and separate scaling at its
right endpoint. The first analytic start is below $10^8$.
For the new $1/8$ finite tradeoffs there is a **new exact
tape** through 250000000 (right terminal endpoint included),
then finite20b bands through $2\cdot10^{10}$, and then
the same analytic covering from $L=23.7$, strictly below
$\log(2\cdot10^{10})$. Both sets of the latter bands/cells
pass even .001323. The analytic continuation after $59.5$
is as above. The additional five levels are re-sieved in
`d02finite_repair.cpp` with the same interval proof and cutoffs;
`repair_tape.txt` preserves the old bands and threshold results
and supplies the new power levels.

**New tape details.** `d02finite.cpp` is the proof-preserving
segmented sieve in `finite.md` with finer cells and a new
scaling guard. All composites are erased at their least prime
factor (the factor is included among the base primes); the
stored cumulative values are built in the original fixed-point
units $S=2^{56}$. Interval proof for interpolation and the
exact $\gamma,M,B_3$ normalization constants, including
truncated tail brackets, is in `finite.md`. On $[u,v$)
exclude a possible prime at $v$ from the upper-state
prefix. Subtract independent baseline intervals accounting
for the *entire* cell. The terminal cell includes $v=N$.
For the new guard use the upper $L_v$ scaling and
$e^{L_v/8}$, directed in fixed point, degree 34 for
argument in $[0,3]$; the omitted tail is
$<2\cdot3^{35}/35!<2^{-56}$. Products use
$e^{|\delta_Q|}-1\le |\delta_Q|+|\delta_Q|^2/
[2(1-|\delta_Q|/3)]$, by the factorial series. For each
coefficient store the last right endpoint of a failed sufficient
guard, then **start at** that endpoint, which belongs to
the subsequent passing half-open cell. The output shows
no failure at the terminal test at any new level. A failed
cell need not contain an actual violation.
The tape also gives independent finer B0 bands and
$k/100$ thresholds for $k=4,\ldots,30$ in the old
logarithmic shapes on whole rays; after 250000000 use the
older passing finite20b certificates (all of their last
failures for these rows are below the join), then
the inherited .0077 log-polynomial estimate through infinity.
The $k<4$ rows in that new tape are at most *bounded-domain*
claims there. The $1/8$ power continuation at the much
smaller coefficient .001354, unlike the finite computation
itself, is owed to the D02 tail.

    x,hi,step=F(lo),F(hi),F(step)
    worst=I(0)
    while x<hi:
        y=min(x+step,hi)
        mode=0 if y<=F('29.9') else 1 if y<=F('43.7') else 2
        assert not any(x<t<y for t in [F('29.9'),F('43.7')])
        v=I(d01scale(x,y,mode,plain=True).U())*I(y)**q*e(I(y)*alpha)
        worst=maxI(worst,v)
        x=y
    return worst

def bands(path,start,end,alpha,q):
    worst=I(0); start,end=F(start),F(end)
    join=start
    for ln in Path(path).read_text().splitlines():
        if not ln.startswith('['): continue
        ls,rs=ln[1:].split('] : ')
        aa,bb=map(int,ls.split(','))
        lb,ub=max(aa,start),min(bb,end)
        if lb>=ub:continue
        assert lb==join
        k=max(map(int,rs.split()))
        worst=maxI(worst,*(I(k)/10**9*log(x)**(q-2)*e(alpha*log(x)) for x in [lb,ub]))
        join=ub
    assert join==end

source_references.readback:
**Boundary-zero obstruction (not existence).** Termwise
bounded convergence in the *absolutely* summable high
strip, with FKS's signed formula and growing cutoff,
gives the leading possible spectral term
$$
 e^{aL}e_{\psi}(L)=-2\Re \sum_{\beta=b,\,\gamma>0}e^{i\gamma L}/\rho+o(1).
$$
Indeed the density screen is summable at $s_*$; each term
with $\beta<b$ goes to zero after scaling, and low-strip
and truncation losses go to zero. Smoothed transfer or the
combined-pole formula shows that the corresponding leading
term for $e^{aL}\delta_V, Le^{aL}\delta_S, Le^{aL}\delta_Q$
has denominator $\rho-1$ instead, and the products have
opposite signs after linearization. This does not assert any
boundary zeros. A further logarithmic saving at the same
power (little-o of the current shape) would exclude them:
reverse partial summation on $U_1=\sum Lambda(n)/n$ or
$U_0=\sum Lambda(n)/(n\log n)$, adding the smaller prime-power
corrections, to get $\psi(x)-x=o(x^b)$.
For $U_1$ integrate against $t$, and for $U_0$ against
$t\log t$; the main derivatives give $x+O(1)$, and
the boundary and integrated little-o terms are both
$o(x^b)$. For products the logarithm preserves little-o
near 1. At $s=\rho+\epsilon$ in the Mellin formula of D02.md
the integral times $\epsilon$ then tends to 0, contradicting
a logarithmic-derivative pole at a zero with $\Re\rho=b$.
A fixed gain in exponent with any fixed log power would
force a smaller zero strip by the same continuation argument.

def combined(L,B=b):
    x=I(L); alpha=1-B
    J,J2=smooth(L,alpha)
    Y=(F(27,100) if B==b else F(7,20))*x
    v=screen(L,B,c=F(7,20))+2*(Y+1)*e(-Y)/PI+2*e(-B*x)
    z=v+J/x+2*(1/x+2/x**2)*J2+2*e(-(F(1,2)-alpha)*x)+x*e(-B*x)
    return z/(1-z*e(-alpha*x)/x)

following operations can be added on the same domain without
new analytic hypotheses. For a nonnegative decreasing
differentiable $f$ with $tf(t)\to0$, let

**Extremal totient ratio.** For $(L_0,c)=(169,.513)$ or
$(174,.4982)$ and every real $N$ with $\log\log N\ge L_0$,
$$
\left|e^{-\gamma}\max_{1\le n\le N,\ n\in\mathbb N}
     n/\varphi(n)-\log\log N\right|<c(\log N)^{-a}.
$$
Set $Y=\log N,u=Y^{-a}$ and $t_\pm=Y(1\pm d u)$.
For $L_0=169$ use cap $C=.256418$ and $d=.2565$; for
$174$ use $C=.249,d=.2491$. Then $\log t_\pm\ge L_0-1$.
The certified theta inequalities with coefficient $C$
at exponent $b$ imply $\theta(t_-)<Y<\theta(t_+)$ by
$(1+v)^b\le1+v$ for $v\ge0$ and $C(1+du)<d$.
The primorial through $t_-$ is available and the one
through $t_+$ is not. At fixed cardinality the smallest
primes minimize the product and maximize the totient
ratio, so the extremum lies between $Q(t_-)$ and $Q(t_+)$.
Using Mertens' cap $C$ on the same domain and
$|\log(1\pm du)|\le du/(1-du)$, $t_\pm^{-a}\le u/(1-du)$,
the normalized additive error is at most $(C+d)u/(1-du)<cu$.
It also bounds $\sigma(n)/n$ from above via finite geometric
sums. Both new shapes improve the old .02635 bound at
the $1/8$ exponent from the common loglog start 181 by the
ratio test, retaining earlier or weaker-premise tradeoffs.

for L0,cap,shift,bound in [(169,'.256418','.2565','.513'),
                               (174,'.249','.2491','.4982')]:
        L=I(L0); u=e(-a*L)
        C,D,Q=I(cap),I(shift),I(bound)
        assert combined(F(L0-1))<C
        assert screen(F(L0-1),c=F(7,20))+3*e(-(F(1,2)-a)*I(L0-1))<C
        assert log(1-D*u)>-1
        assert C*(1+D*u)<D
        assert (D+C)/(1-D*u)<Q
        assert Q*e(-I(181)/32)<I('.02635')

source_references.readback:
**Correlated endpoints, improved logarithmic factor.** For
every real $x\ge e^{100000}$, let
$$
 g=x^{5/8}L^{207/20},\qquad y=x+g .
$$
Then $\pi(y)-\pi(x)>.81g/\log y$.
This replaces the inherited exponent 14 of $L$ at the same
onset by 10.35, and raises the constant in units of the
new shorter length (not a comparison of absolute counts
in two different intervals).

Here are analytic and numerical details. Put
$k=207/20, \delta=g/x, Z=3/\delta, z=\log Z
=3L/8-k\log L+\log3$, $s_0=5/8+1/L$.
For $L\ge100000$ we have $0<\delta<1, L/3<z<2L/5, Z>H$.
Use the FKS signed formula at each endpoint $v=x,y$,
with $T_v=v^{2/5}$. Its cutoff is at least $Z$, and is
below $v$; the admissibility inequalities follow at these
heights as in D02.md §3. For $\beta \ge s_0$,
$$
 |(y^{\rho}-x^{\rho})/\rho|
       \le x^{\beta} \min(\delta,3/|\gamma|).
$$
Use the integral of the derivative for the first bound
and $1+(y/x)^{\beta} \le3$ for the second. For $s\ge s_0$
the density sums converge absolutely since $p(s)<1$.
In passing from the truncated to the full high sums the
two omitted endpoint tails together cost at most **one
more** absolute sum of the same positive weights: for each
omitted ordinate $\gamma>Z$ the weight is $3x^{\beta}/\gamma$,
and $x^{\beta}+y^{\beta} \le3x^{\beta}$.
The high cost is thus at most twice the full absolute
difference bound.

In the union of the relevant FKS Table 8 first-panel intervals
$5/8\le s\le b$ one can take $c\le12,d\le6$.
Set $\lambda=1-p, p=(8/3)(1-s), q=3+3p/4$.
The two-sided mass for $\min(\delta,3/\gamma)$ in the
tail above $s$ is at most $3V(s,z)$, where
$$
 V(s,z)=\frac{2c e^{-\lambda z}z^q}{\lambda}
            \sum_{j=0}^4(4)_j/(\lambda z)^j
                  +2d e^{-z}(z^2+2z+2).
$$
Indeed integrate $2 N(s,t)$ with $dt/t^2$ from $Z$,
since $3/Z=\delta$; and use
$(1+w/z)^q\le(1+w/z)^4$ with $t=Ze^w$.
Here $(4)_j=4!/(4-j)!$.
Using $\lambda z\ge8/9$, the sum is $<100$,
and for $s\ge.75$ it is $<2$ using $\lambda z\ge L/9$.
The first term is respectively
$\le900 L z^q e^{-\lambda z}$ and
$\le144 z^q e^{-\lambda z}$.

Rather than summing independent unit log-bins, integrate
the **layer-cake** tail. On each substrip $[u,v]$ from
$s_0$ to .75 or from .75 to $b$ the bound is
$$
 3x^u V(u,z)+3L\int_u^v x^s V(s,z)\,ds.
$$
Endpoint atoms can be assigned to either piece, or use a
closed-bin cumulative bound by continuity from the left.
The density integral at any fixed numerical table join
is bounded by either one-sided continuous table majorant,
so no assumption about zeros on such joins is used.
The identity $x^s e^{-\lambda z}/g=3^{-\lambda}L^{-kp}$
simplifies this integral. Use $z^q\le(.4)^3 L^q$.
For the substrip below .75 use $p\ge2/3$ and its length
at most $1/8$. For the upper substrip integrate the affine
exponent exactly:
$$
 \int_{.75}^b L^{3-(k-.75)p(s)}\,ds
 \le L^{3-(k-.75)p(b)} /[(8/3)(k-.75)\log L].
$$
Now $p(b)=5/12$ and $(k-.75)p(b)=4$.
The resulting upper bound for the high contribution
divided by $g$, **before** doubling, is
$$
 172.8(1+L/8)L^{-12/5}
 +27.648(L^{-17/5}+1/(25.6\log L))
 +12(L^2+2L+2)(2+L)e^{-aL}.
$$
The last term includes both substrips' second terms
using $3x^s e^{-z}/g\le e^{-aL}$.

By the total reciprocal bound in D02.md §3 the low portion,
FKS truncation and prime powers at both endpoints together
cost at most
$$
 L^{-k}\{4e[(L+1)^2/6+3]+8.364(L+1)e^{-L/40}+9e^{-L/8}\}
$$
in units of $g$, using $\log y\le L+1$,
$y^{s_0}\le2e x^{5/8}$, $y^{.6}\le2x^{.6}$.
Each term bounding these losses decreases from $L=100000$.
The exact arithmetic guard there gives sum of the doubled
high and other terms $<.19$. Thus $\theta(y)-\theta(x)>.81g$,
and each counted prime weighs at most $\log y$.
The cutoff cancellation and the new cap, not subtraction of
two unsigned estimates, are necessary in this proof.

# Correlated short interval with log power 207/20.
    L=I(100000); k=F(207,20)
    z=3*L/8-k*log(L)+log(3)
    assert L/3<z and z<2*L/5 and z>h
    assert k/L<F(1,24) and log(3)<L/40
    assert k*log(L)<3*L/8 and k/L<F(3,8)
    assert sum(I(fac(j)*comb(4,j))*F(9,8)**j for j in range(5))<100
    assert sum(I(fac(j)*comb(4,j))*(9/L)**j for j in range(5))<2
    assert I('.4')**3*3*144<I('27.649')
    low=I('172.8')*(1+L/8)*e((-F(12,5))*log(L))

def fixed_prime_guard(flag,a,b,A,constants,j,c,unit=U):
    """Endpoint certification on constant-prime-state pieces of [a,b]."""
    assert a>=START
    if not exact_scaled_ok(a,A,constants,j,c,unit):
        return False
    p=flag.find(b'\1',a+1,b+1)
    while p!=-1:
        if not exact_scaled_ok(p,A,constants,j,c,unit):
            return False
        A,_,_=add(A,p)
        if not exact_scaled_ok(p,A,constants,j,c,unit):
            return False
        p=flag.find(b'\1',p+1,b+1)
    return exact_scaled_ok(b,A,constants,j,c,unit)

def end_analysis(flag,tape,constants):
    tab=[W3,W3,W2]
    got=[[START]*len(W) for W in tab]
    a,A=tape[0]
    F=lp_data(a)
    fail=[0,0,0]
    stats=[0,0,0]
    goals=(1999990,1999990,2999995)
    baseline_onset=(P0,S0,V0)
    base_mx=[0,0,0]
    for b,Q in tape[1:]:
        Z=lp_data(b)
        ce=coef(residuals(A,Q,F,Z,constants),Z[1])
        for j in range(3):
            for i in range(bisect_left(tab[j],ce[j])):
                c=tab[j][i]
                # Refine only reasonably close cells; a failed guard may
                # conservatively move the onset later and never weakens proof.
                if ce[j]-c > 16000 or not fixed_prime_guard(flag,a,b,A,constants,j,c):
                    got[j][i]=b
            if a>=baseline_onset[j] and 10*ce[j]>goals[j]:
                stats[j]+=1
                if not fixed_prime_guard(flag,a,b,A,constants,j,goals[j],10*U):
                    fail[j]+=1
                    base_mx[j]=b
        a,A,F=b,Q,Z
    print("columns c (millionths), certified onset:", flush=True)
    for j in range(3):
        print(j,list(zip(tab[j],got[j])),flush=True)
        assert all(x<N for x in got[j])
    print("original-onset refinement cells:",stats, "failures:",fail,
          "last failed end:",base_mx,flush=True)
    return got,fail,base_mx

def root_proof(flag,st):
    """The exact sharp real onset for error 0.2/L^3 in product family."""
    assert not flag[P0]
    ql=st[0]+st[2]
    qh=st[0]+st[1]+st[3]
    r=P0*10**9
    l=(P0-1)*10**9
    d=10**9
    def which(x):
        flo,fhi,ll,lh=lp_data(x,d)
        zlo=ql-GHI-lh
        zhi=qh-GLO-ll
        assert 0<zlo<=zhi<B//100
        a,_=lg(5*fhi**3+B**3,5*fhi**3)
        _,b=lg(5*flo**3+B**3,5*flo**3)
        if zlo>b:
            return 1
        if zhi<a:
            return -1
        return 0
    assert which(l)==1 and which(r)==-1
    while r-l>1:
        mid=(l+r)//2
        w=which(mid)
        if w==0:
            break
        if w>0:
            l=mid
        else:
            r=mid
    assert r-l<=10
    print("sharp 0.2 product onset bracket /10^9:",l,r,flush=True)

def sum_roots(flag,tape,constants):
    d=10**4
    for end,j,target in [(S0,1,2),(V0,2,3)]:
        assert not flag[end]
        Q=next(st for x,st in tape if x==end)
        def w(x):
            F=lp_data(x,d)
            zlo,zhi=residuals(Q,Q,F,F,constants)[j]
            k=4-j
            assert zlo>0 and zhi<B//100
            if 10*zlo*F[0]**k>target*B**(k+1):
                return 1
            if 10*zhi*F[1]**k<target*B**(k+1):
                return -1
            return 0
        a,b=(end-1)*d,end*d
        assert w(a)==1 and w(b)==-1
        while b-a>1:
            m=(a+b)//2
            c=w(m)
            if c==0:
                if m>a+1 and w(m-1)==1: a=m-1
                if m<b-1 and w(m+1)==-1: b=m+1
                break
            if c>0: a=m
            else: b=m
        assert b-a<=3
        print("sharp sum onset (column, bracket /10^4):",j,a,b,flush=True)
    Q=next(st for x,st in tape if x==V0)
    F=lp_data(V0)
    z=residuals(Q,Q,F,F,constants)[2][0]
    assert z>0 and U*z*F[0]**2>299999*B**3  # earlier failed target is false

def main():
    flag=sieve(N)
    A=(0,0,0,0,0,0)
    tape=[]
    p=2
    lo=hi=0
    a=START
    rootst=None
    while True:
        while p>=0 and p<=a:
            A,l,r=add(A,p)
            lo+=l
            hi+=r
            p=flag.find(b'\1',p+1)
        tape.append((a,A))
        if a==P0:
            rootst=A
        if a==N:
            break
        a=min(a+max(1,a//25000),CUTS[bisect_left(CUTS,a+1)])
    assert rootst is not None and p==-1
    print("sieve primes:",A[1],"cells:",len(tape)-1,flush=True)
    assert tape[-1][0]==N
    # Uses proved uniform |theta(t)-t| <= t/5000 on t >= N.
    wl,wh=lg(N,N-1)
    pad=cd(cd(2*B,N-1)+wh,5000)
    bl,bh=GLO+lo+wl-pad,GHI+hi+wh+pad
    lnlo,lnhi=lg(N)
    curlo=curhi=0
    for j in range(13):
        jlo=(factorial(j)*B**(j+2))//(2*N*lnhi**(j+1))
        jhi=cd(factorial(j)*B**(j+2),2*N*lnlo**(j+1))
        if j%2:
            curlo-=jhi
            curhi-=jlo
        else:
            curlo+=jlo
            curhi+=jhi
        if j==11:
            il=curlo
    ih=curhi
    pad=cd(cd(B*B,N*lnlo)+ih,5000)
    ml=GLO-A[3]-ih-pad-cd(B,3*N*N)
    mh=GHI-A[2]-il+pad
    print("exact constants /2^80:", (GLO,GHI),(ml,mh),(bl,bh),flush=True)
    root_proof(flag,rootst)
    sum_roots(flag,tape,(ml,mh,bl,bh))
    got,fail,last=end_analysis(flag,tape,(ml,mh,bl,bh))
    assert got[0][W3.index(125000)]<=7_250_000
    assert got[1][W3.index(125000)]<=7_250_000
    assert got[2][W2.index(135000)]<=7_250_000
    assert fail==[0,0,0]

B0=F('29.9')
L0=F('18.42')
def finite_mertens_checks():
    # Mid-range bound prior to FKS unconditional tail splice.
    aa0=A
    # Power bound from v=3000 using FKS Corollary 1.4 and prime powers.
    K=3000
    k=isqrt(K*10**12)
    xl=F(k,10**6)
    xu=F(k+1,10**6)
    assert (F('9.22022')*K**4*xu*up(-F('0.8476836')*xl)
            +3*K**3*up(-F(K,2)))<F('0.0003')
    # Uniform strong psi/theta majorant used for finite constants.
    assert F('0.751')+F('1.000000147')+F('1.78')*up(-L0/6)<F('1.84')
    assert F('1.84')*up(-L0/2)<F(1,5000)
    assert B0**2*up(-B0/2)/25<F(1,5000)
    assert aa0+117*up(-F(58,2))<F(1,5000)
    # Tail integration on [58,3000] + [3000,infinity).
    Ihi=aa0*(K-58)+234*up(-F(58,2))+F('0.0003')/(2*K*K)
    Jhi=(1+F(1,58))/58*Ihi
    # FRH tail from B0 onwards, beyond the CH2 splice pessimistically added.
    I=up(-B0/2)*(2*B0**2+8*B0+16)/25+Ihi
    J=up(-B0/2)*(2*B0+6)/25+Jhi
    # phi=theta/x-1 is nonpositive in the range in which the first line
    # is used. Lower error from boundary only plus far tail.
    I39=up(-F(39,2))*(2*39**2+8*39+16)/25+Ihi
    J39=up(-F(39,2))*(2*39+6)/25+Jhi
    def e2(l):return F('1.751000147')*up(-l/2)+F('1.78')*up(-F(2,3)*l)
    # I and J prime-counting tails normalized by L^2 or L^3.
    for l,r in grid(L0,B0,F(1,50)):
        i=r**2*(2*F('1.751000147')*up(-l/2)+F('2.67')*up(-F(2,3)*l)+I)
        # w3=(1+v)/v^2. At exponent 1/2, integral <=
        # e^-L/2 (2/L - 2/L^2 + 8/L^3).
        # At exponent 2/3 use I1+I2 <= e^-fL/(fL).
        j=r**3*(F('1.751000147')*up(-l/2)*(2/l-2/l**2+8/l**3)
                 +F('2.67')*up(-F(2,3)*l)/l+J)
        ilo=r**2*(e2(l)+I39)
        jlo=r**3*(e2(l)/l+J39+up(-l))
        assert max(i,ilo)<F('0.135'),(l,r,"V")
        # Conservative conversion exp(z)-1 <= z/(1-z).
        h=max(j,jlo)
        assert h/(1-h/l**3)<F('0.125'),(l,r,"Q")
    # B0 <= L <=58: normalized triangle maxima at B0 for the decaying
    # FRH terms, and 58 for the later tail constants.
    i=(3*B0**2+8*B0+16)*up(-B0/2)*B0**2/25+58**2*Ihi
    j=(3*B0+6)*up(-B0/2)*B0**3/25+58**3*(Jhi+up(-B0))
    assert i<F('0.135') and j/(1-j/B0**3)<F('0.125')
    # 58 <= L <= 3000: use monotonically decreasing exponential times
    # L^2 at 58 and global fixed constant tails.
    u=(aa0+aa0*(K-58)+F('0.0003')/(2*K*K))*K*K+351*58**2*up(-F(58,2))
    assert u<F('0.135')
    # T_3 <= w_3(L) T_2 and B_3 = B_2/L.
    v=(1+F(1,58))*u+58**3*up(-58)
    assert v/(1-v/58**3)<F('0.125')
    # L >= 3000: d <= .0003/L^3.
    u=F('0.0003')*(F(1,K)+F(1,2))
    v=(1+F(1,K))*u+F(1,10**6)  # bound L^3 e^-L using L>=3000
    assert u<F('0.135') and v/(1-v/K**3)<F('0.125')
    print("unconditional Mertens rays passed")

    assert a>=START

def fixed_prime_guard(flag,a,b,A,constants,j,c,unit=U):
    """Endpoint certification on constant-prime-state pieces of [a,b]."""
    assert a>=START
    if not exact_scaled_ok(a,A,constants,j,c,unit):
        return False
    p=flag.find(b'\1',a+1,b+1)
    while p!=-1:
        if not exact_scaled_ok(p,A,constants,j,c,unit):
            return False
        A,_,_=add(A,p)
        if not exact_scaled_ok(p,A,constants,j,c,unit):
            return False
        p=flag.find(b'\1',p+1,b+1)
    return exact_scaled_ok(b,A,constants,j,c,unit)

    a,A=tape[0]

    fail=[0,0,0]
    stats=[0,0,0]
    goals=(1999990,1999990,2999995)
    baseline_onset=(P0,S0,V0)
    base_mx=[0,0,0]
    for b,Q in tape[1:]:
        Z=lp_data(b)

                c=tab[j][i]

                stats[j]+=1

                    fail[j]+=1

        a,A,F=b,Q,Z
    print("columns c (millionths), certified onset:", flush=True)

    """The exact sharp real onset for error 0.2/L^3 in product family."""
    assert not flag[P0]
    ql=st[0]+st[2]
    qh=st[0]+st[1]+st[3]
    r=P0*10**9
    l=(P0-1)*10**9
    d=10**9
    def which(x):
        flo,fhi,ll,lh=lp_data(x,d)
        zlo=ql-GHI-lh
        zhi=qh-GLO-ll
        assert 0<zlo<=zhi<B//100
        a,_=lg(5*fhi**3+B**3,5*fhi**3)
        _,b=lg(5*flo**3+B**3,5*flo**3)
        if zlo>b:
            return 1
        if zhi<a:
            return -1
        return 0
    assert which(l)==1 and which(r)==-1
    while r-l>1:
        mid=(l+r)//2
        w=which(mid)
        if w==0:
            break
        if w>0:
            l=mid
        else:
            r=mid
    assert r-l<=10

    d=10**4

        assert not flag[end]
        Q=next(st for x,st in tape if x==end)
        def w(x):
            F=lp_data(x,d)
            zlo,zhi=residuals(Q,Q,F,F,constants)[j]
            k=4-j
            assert zlo>0 and zhi<B//100
            if 10*zlo*F[0]**k>target*B**(k+1):
                return 1
            if 10*zhi*F[1]**k<target*B**(k+1):
                return -1
            return 0
        a,b=(end-1)*d,end*d
        assert w(a)==1 and w(b)==-1
        while b-a>1:
            m=(a+b)//2
            c=w(m)
            if c==0:
                if m>a+1 and w(m-1)==1: a=m-1
                if m<b-1 and w(m+1)==-1: b=m+1
                break
            if c>0: a=m

        if not exact_scaled_ok(p,A,constants,j,c,unit):

        if not exact_scaled_ok(p,A,constants,j,c,unit):

    fail=[0,0,0]

    qh=st[0]+st[1]+st[3]

    l=(P0-1)*10**9
    d=10**9
    def which(x):
        flo,fhi,ll,lh=lp_data(x,d)
        zlo=ql-GHI-lh
        zhi=qh-GLO-ll
        assert 0<zlo<=zhi<B//100
        a,_=lg(5*fhi**3+B**3,5*fhi**3)
        _,b=lg(5*flo**3+B**3,5*flo**3)
        if zlo>b:
            return 1
        if zhi<a:
            return -1
        return 0
    assert which(l)==1 and which(r)==-1
    while r-l>1:
        mid=(l+r)//2
        w=which(mid)
        if w==0:
            break

            l=mid

    d=10**4
    for end,j,target in [(S0,1,2),(V0,2,3)]:
        assert not flag[end]
        Q=next(st for x,st in tape if x==end)
        def w(x):
            F=lp_data(x,d)
            zlo,zhi=residuals(Q,Q,F,F,constants)[j]
            k=4-j
            assert zlo>0 and zhi<B//100
            if 10*zlo*F[0]**k>target*B**(k+1):
                return 1
            if 10*zhi*F[1]**k<target*B**(k+1):
                return -1
            return 0
        a,b=(end-1)*d,end*d
        assert w(a)==1 and w(b)==-1
        while b-a>1:
            m=(a+b)//2
            c=w(m)
            if c==0:
                if m>a+1 and w(m-1)==1: a=m-1
                if m<b-1 and w(m+1)==-1: b=m+1
                break
            if c>0: a=m

        if not exact_scaled_ok(p,A,constants,j,c,unit):

        if not exact_scaled_ok(p,A,constants,j,c,unit):

    a,A=tape[0]

    fail=[0,0,0]
    stats=[0,0,0]
    goals=(1999990,1999990,2999995)
    baseline_onset=(P0,S0,V0)
    base_mx=[0,0,0]
    for b,Q in tape[1:]:

    """The exact sharp real onset for error 0.2/L^3 in product family."""
    assert not flag[P0]
    ql=st[0]+st[2]
    qh=st[0]+st[1]+st[3]
    r=P0*10**9
    l=(P0-1)*10**9
    d=10**9
    def which(x):
        flo,fhi,ll,lh=lp_data(x,d)
        zlo=ql-GHI-lh
        zhi=qh-GLO-ll
        assert 0<zlo<=zhi<B//100
        a,_=lg(5*fhi**3+B**3,5*fhi**3)
        _,b=lg(5*flo**3+B**3,5*flo**3)
        if zlo>b:
            return 1
        if zhi<a:
            return -1
        return 0
    assert which(l)==1 and which(r)==-1
    while r-l>1:
        mid=(l+r)//2
        w=which(mid)
        if w==0:
            break
        if w>0:
            l=mid

    d=10**4

        assert not flag[end]
        Q=next(st for x,st in tape if x==end)
        def w(x):
            F=lp_data(x,d)
            zlo,zhi=residuals(Q,Q,F,F,constants)[j]
            k=4-j
            assert zlo>0 and zhi<B//100
            if 10*zlo*F[0]**k>target*B**(k+1):
                return 1
            if 10*zhi*F[1]**k<target*B**(k+1):
                return -1
            return 0
        a,b=(end-1)*d,end*d
        assert w(a)==1 and w(b)==-1
        while b-a>1:
            m=(a+b)//2
            c=w(m)
            if c==0:
                if m>a+1 and w(m-1)==1: a=m-1
                if m<b-1 and w(m+1)==-1: b=m+1
                break
            if c>0: a=m

    l=(P0-1)*10**9
    d=10**9

        flo,fhi,ll,lh=lp_data(x,d)
        zlo=ql-GHI-lh
        zhi=qh-GLO-ll
        assert 0<zlo<=zhi<B//100
        a,_=lg(5*fhi**3+B**3,5*fhi**3)
        _,b=lg(5*flo**3+B**3,5*flo**3)

            return 1
        if zhi<a:

        return 0
    assert which(l)==1 and which(r)==-1

            F=lp_data(x,d)

            k=4-j
            assert zlo>0 and zhi<B//100
            if 10*zlo*F[0]**k>target*B**(k+1):

                return -1
            return 0

def fixed_prime_guard(flag,a,b,A,constants,j,c,unit=U):
    """Endpoint certification on constant-prime-state pieces of [a,b]."""
    assert a>=START
    if not exact_scaled_ok(a,A,constants,j,c,unit):
        return False
    p=flag.find(b'\1',a+1,b+1)
    while p!=-1:
        if not exact_scaled_ok(p,A,constants,j,c,unit):
            return False
        A,_,_=add(A,p)
        if not exact_scaled_ok(p,A,constants,j,c,unit):
            return False
        p=flag.find(b'\1',p+1,b+1)
    return exact_scaled_ok(b,A,constants,j,c,unit)

def end_analysis(flag,tape,constants):
    tab=[W3,W3,W2]
    got=[[START]*len(W) for W in tab]
    a,A=tape[0]
    F=lp_data(a)
    fail=[0,0,0]
    stats=[0,0,0]
    goals=(1999990,1999990,2999995)
    baseline_onset=(P0,S0,V0)
    base_mx=[0,0,0]
    for b,Q in tape[1:]:
        Z=lp_data(b)
        ce=coef(residuals(A,Q,F,Z,constants),Z[1])
        for j in range(3):
            for i in range(bisect_left(tab[j],ce[j])):
                c=tab[j][i]
                # Refine only reasonably close cells; a failed guard may
                # conservatively move the onset later and never weakens proof.
                if ce[j]-c > 16000 or not fixed_prime_guard(flag,a,b,A,constants,j,c):
                    got[j][i]=b
            if a>=baseline_onset[j] and 10*ce[j]>goals[j]:
                stats[j]+=1
                if not fixed_prime_guard(flag,a,b,A,constants,j,goals[j],10*U):
                    fail[j]+=1
                    base_mx[j]=b
        a,A,F=b,Q,Z
    print("columns c (millionths), certified onset:", flush=True)
    for j in range(3):
        print(j,list(zip(tab[j],got[j])),flush=True)
        assert all(x<N for x in got[j])
    print("original-onset refinement cells:",stats, "failures:",fail,
          "last failed end:",base_mx,flush=True)
    return got,fail,base_mx

def root_proof(flag,st):
    """The exact sharp real onset for error 0.2/L^3 in product family."""
    assert not flag[P0]
    ql=st[0]+st[2]
    qh=st[0]+st[1]+st[3]
    r=P0*10**9
    l=(P0-1)*10**9
    d=10**9
    def which(x):
        flo,fhi,ll,lh=lp_data(x,d)
        zlo=ql-GHI-lh
        zhi=qh-GLO-ll
        assert 0<zlo<=zhi<B//100
        a,_=lg(5*fhi**3+B**3,5*fhi**3)
        _,b=lg(5*flo**3+B**3,5*flo**3)
        if zlo>b:
            return 1
        if zhi<a:
            return -1
        return 0
    assert which(l)==1 and which(r)==-1
    while r-l>1:
        mid=(l+r)//2
        w=which(mid)
        if w==0:
            break
        if w>0:
            l=mid
        else:
            r=mid
    assert r-l<=10
    print("sharp 0.2 product onset bracket /10^9:",l,r,flush=True)

def sum_roots(flag,tape,constants):
    d=10**4
    for end,j,target in [(S0,1,2),(V0,2,3)]:
        assert not flag[end]
        Q=next(st for x,st in tape if x==end)
        def w(x):
            F=lp_data(x,d)
            zlo,zhi=residuals(Q,Q,F,F,constants)[j]
            k=4-j
            assert zlo>0 and zhi<B//100
            if 10*zlo*F[0]**k>target*B**(k+1):
                return 1
            if 10*zhi*F[1]**k<target*B**(k+1):
                return -1
            return 0
        a,b=(end-1)*d,end*d
        assert w(a)==1 and w(b)==-1
        while b-a>1:
            m=(a+b)//2
            c=w(m)
            if c==0:
                if m>a+1 and w(m-1)==1: a=m-1
                if m<b-1 and w(m+1)==-1: b=m+1
                break
            if c>0: a=m
            else: b=m
        assert b-a<=3
        print("sharp sum onset (column, bracket /10^4):",j,a,b,flush=True)
    Q=next(st for x,st in tape if x==V0)
    F=lp_data(V0)
    z=residuals(Q,Q,F,F,constants)[2][0]
    assert z>0 and U*z*F[0]**2>299999*B**3  # earlier failed target is false

def main():
    flag=sieve(N)
    A=(0,0,0,0,0,0)
    tape=[]
    p=2
    lo=hi=0
    a=START
    rootst=None
    while True:
        while p>=0 and p<=a:
            A,l,r=add(A,p)
            lo+=l
            hi+=r
            p=flag.find(b'\1',p+1)
        tape.append((a,A))
        if a==P0:
            rootst=A
        if a==N:
            break
        a=min(a+max(1,a//25000),CUTS[bisect_left(CUTS,a+1)])
    assert rootst is not None and p==-1
    print("sieve primes:",A[1],"cells:",len(tape)-1,flush=True)
    assert tape[-1][0]==N
    # Uses proved uniform |theta(t)-t| <= t/5000 on t >= N.
    wl,wh=lg(N,N-1)
    pad=cd(cd(2*B,N-1)+wh,5000)
    bl,bh=GLO+lo+wl-pad,GHI+hi+wh+pad
    lnlo,lnhi=lg(N)
    curlo=curhi=0
    for j in range(13):
        jlo=(factorial(j)*B**(j+2))//(2*N*lnhi**(j+1))
        jhi=cd(factorial(j)*B**(j+2),2*N*lnlo**(j+1))
        if j%2:
            curlo-=jhi
            curhi-=jlo
        else:
            curlo+=jlo
            curhi+=jhi
        if j==11:
            il=curlo
    ih=curhi
    pad=cd(cd(B*B,N*lnlo)+ih,5000)
    ml=GLO-A[3]-ih-pad-cd(B,3*N*N)
    mh=GHI-A[2]-il+pad
    print("exact constants /2^80:", (GLO,GHI),(ml,mh),(bl,bh),flush=True)
    root_proof(flag,rootst)
    sum_roots(flag,tape,(ml,mh,bl,bh))
    got,fail,last=end_analysis(flag,tape,(ml,mh,bl,bh))
    assert got[0][W3.index(125000)]<=7_250_000
    assert got[1][W3.index(125000)]<=7_250_000
    assert got[2][W2.index(135000)]<=7_250_000
    assert fail==[0,0,0]
